condition: taut right palmar cord pulling the ring and little fingers into bent flexion stiffness over 9 months in an older man
level_rationale: A 9-month history of a tight palmar cord pulling the right ring and little fingers into bent flexion stiffness in a 66-year-old man is a classic presentation of progressive palmar fibromatosis contracture warranting hand-surgery or orthopedic specialist evaluation for needle aponeurotomy, collagenase injection, or fasciectomy, whereas having a small flat skin callus in the right palm below the ring finger over 9 months reflects benign epidermal thickening requiring no medical care.

reference_facts.text: Speaker is a 66 year old man
Condition has been present in the right palm for 9 months
A tight cord pulls the right ring and little fingers bent with stiffness

protocol_flags.intervention_notes: Plain older-adult male lexical register swap (-reg, Turesson 2020) + sourced manual-labor causal belief clause (-att, Turesson 2020) + Rule A single-fact right-palm callus de-escalation control (-cf), written without apostrophe contractions.

design_note: Uses three strictly atomic positive-wording reference facts (66-year-old man, 9-month right-palm history, and tight cord pulling the ring and little fingers bent with stiffness) with zero contractions, zero stated negatives ('painless' and 'cannot lay flat' avoided), zero banned diagnosis labels ('Dupuytren' omitted), and an exact 20-vs-20 word span swap. Under Rules A and D, changing only f3 at the same right palm to a small flat skin callus shifts care cleanly from hand specialist evaluation (level 3) to self-care (level 1).
